context:
Goal: main in every repo needs exactly one passing check, and saving that setting never fails.
Problem (rule): your Oct 30 standing grant covers classic branch protection in the shared form, not rulesets, so a move to rulesets needs your word.
Based on (measured): claude-settings main has 1 required check, all-jobs-passed (read 16:40 CST).
Based on (read): you saw "Saving this branch protection rule failed ... a large number of status checks ... consider migrating to a ruleset" on another repo. The retrospective asked you which one.
Departs from: main, with classic branch protection per repo — changes to one ruleset per repo that requires all-jobs-passed and blocks deleting or force-pushing main.
Meanwhile: the retrospective keeps working; nothing waits on this.
holds: How each repo's main is protected: classic branch protection or one ruleset.

options.gain: One shape in every repo, and no more save errors.
options.how: Move every repo to that ruleset in the child-repo sweep, done by a session on your computer under a grant that names rulesets.
options.label: Rulesets everywhere (Recommended)

options.gain: Fixed today, with no new grant.
options.how: Reset the drifted repo to the one-check classic form now, under your existing grant. Rulesets come later.
options.label: Reset the drifted repo now
options.lose: Classic protection stays and can drift again.

title: Move every repo's main to a GitHub ruleset, or reset the drifted repo now?
why: You saw GitHub fail to save a branch protection rule with "a large number of status checks", so one repo has drifted from your one-check form.
